identity.title: Polarization Substructure in the Spiral-dominated HH 111 Disk: Evidence for Grain Growth

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we report the dust polarization results in the disk as well as the inner envelope around it, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array in continuum

targets.name: HH 111 protostellar disk and inner envelope

evidence.quote: located in Orion at a distance of $\sim$ 400 pc

question.value: What produces the dust polarization in the HH 111 inner envelope and spiral-dominated disk (magnetically aligned grains vs dust self-scattering), and does it indicate grain growth

evidence.quote: In order to better determine the origin of the dust polarization, here we report the dust polarization detection at 2.4 times as high resolution and the modeling with the two polarization mechanisms.
ALMA archive Project Code: 2016.1.00389.S

findings_qualitative.value: Polarized intensity and degree are lower in the spiral arms and higher in between the arms

evidence.quote: This suggests an anticorrelation between the spiral arms and the polarized intensity (and thus the polarization degree).

findings_qualitative.value: Inner envelope magnetic field is mainly toroidal

evidence.loc: Origin of the Dust Polarization in the Inner Envelope
evidence.quote: the magnetic fields in the inner envelope are almost everywhere parallel to the major axis and are, thus, mainly toroidal

findings_qualitative.value: Interarms are sandwiched and illuminated by two brighter arms, giving higher scattered polarized intensity

evidence.quote: The interarms are sandwiched and illuminated by two brighter spiral arms and thus have higher polarized intensity.

claims.hypothesis: Is the envelope polarization due to magnetically aligned grains
claims.experiment: Rotated the observed polarization orientations by 90 deg, assuming optically thin emission
claims.result: Polarization is almost everywhere parallel to the minor axis with ~6% degree
claims.finding: Envelope polarization is likely from aligned grains tracing a mainly toroidal field

evidence.loc: Origin of the Dust Polarization in the Inner Envelope
evidence.quote: In this case, the magnetic fields in the inner envelope are almost everywhere parallel to the major axis and are, thus, mainly toroidal

claims.hypothesis: Does the disk polarized intensity correlate with the spiral arms
claims.experiment: Mapped Stokes I and polarized intensity at three resolutions
claims.result: Polarized intensity is lower in the arms and higher in the interarms
claims.finding: The polarized intensity is anticorrelated with the spiral arms, though the inner NE arm is unresolved

evidence.quote: This suggests an anticorrelation between the spiral arms and the polarized intensity (and thus the polarization degree).

claims.hypothesis: Can magnetically aligned grains explain the disk polarization
claims.experiment: Modeled poloidal and toroidal field configurations in the fiducial disk with alpha = 0.1
claims.result: Poloidal fields match only the far-side azimuthal pattern; toroidal fields fail for most orientations; both give polarization along the arms opposite to observed
claims.finding: It is unclear if magnetic alignment explains the disk polarization

evidence.quote: The model with poloidal fields can account only for the azimuthal polarization orientations on the far side, while the model with toroidal fields fails to account for most polarization orientations

claims.hypothesis: Can dust self-scattering explain the disk polarization and indicate grain growth
claims.experiment: RADMC-3D self-scattering model with DSHARP grains of a_max 170 um in the fiducial disk
claims.result: Reproduces ~2% degree, minor-axis orientation on the near side, azimuthal orientation at edges, and the anticorrelation with arms, but not the near-far asymmetry
claims.finding: Polarization is likely dominated by self-scattering by grains grown to ~150 um, with possible contributions from other mechanisms

evidence.quote: Therefore the observed dust polarization in the HH 111 disk is likely dominated by dust self-scattering, with possible contributions from other mechanisms
Thus, our result indicates a grain growth in the disk to a size of $\sim$ 150 $\mu$m.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pure magnetically aligned grains with poloidal or toroidal fields, and their combination, judged inconsistent with the observed orientations

evidence.quote: Adding the toroidal fields into the model with poloidal fields will tilt the polarization orientations to one side (not shown), also inconsistent with the observed polarization orientations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Scattering by aligned (effectively prolate) grains, as proposed for HL Tau, is considered plausible but not modeled

evidence.quote: It is plausible that the polarization observed in our case of HH 111 is also produced by scattering aligned grains.

limitations_admitted.value: Near-far side asymmetry in polarized intensity and far-side azimuthal orientation are not reproduced

evidence.quote: Further modeling work is needed to study how to reproduce the observed near-far side asymmetry in the polarized intensity and the observed azimuthal polarization orientation on the far side.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner NE spiral arm is unresolved, so higher resolution and sensitivity are needed

evidence.quote: observations at higher resolution and sensitivity are needed to confirm it

limitations_admitted.value: Detailed calculations including both emission and scattering by aligned grains are needed to test the scenario quantitatively

evidence.quote: are needed to test the scenario quantitatively

limitations_admitted.value: Model spiral properties and grain properties differ from the actual ones

evidence.quote: The detailed distribution and intensity of the polarized emission are different from the observed polarization map because the actual spirals may have different physical properties

referee_caveats_inferred: Disk model is fit by eye with no uncertainties or degeneracy exploration; opacity, density and temperature are degenerate
Grain size of ~150 um rests on one DSHARP grain demonstration with absorption opacity scaled by a factor of ~2.3, not a fit
Self-scattering vs aligned prolate grains is not uniquely separated; paper itself calls the latter plausible
Effect of phase self-calibration and combining two cycles on polarization fidelity not shown
No polarization at other wavelengths to test the scattering wavelength dependence
